items.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023
items.q: But when I actually played the music with Wallace Roney, I could see the dimensions in it you know

ctx.x: Well see Miles always led the way. See he got tired of playing the same thing anyway. Everywhere he’d go they said, “Play ‘My Funny Valentine’” you know. He didn’t want

to play that no more. And Miles was very fashion oriented you know and the styles were changing you know. And for what it’s worth the music was changing too you know? So he said “In a Silent Way,” I’m going to change. He knew what the barometer was, you know? Because I’ll tell you, I took “Bitches Brew” as a joke you know almost. You know? We put on “Bitches Brew” and rolled a big fat joint and put the color wheel on and strobe light on, and go for a ride. But when I actually played the music with Wallace Roney,…
Yeah he was always ahead of the curve and I’m always fascinated that he was able to fashion the music to his own strengths and weaknesses in his playing.
